title: Managed Data Kit Upgrades: 4-Stage Collision Refactor

stages.scenario: An enterprise with custom Opportunity-to-DMO mappings enables Marketing Cloud Next. The administrator clicks Deploy Sales Data Kit from the setup wizard. Identity Resolution and Calculated Insights fail across the org within minutes. Debugging confirms custom field values no longer reach unified profiles. What is the root cause?

options.text: Marketing Cloud Next requires asynchronous queueable jobs that exceeded the platform daily batch limit.
options.coachingFeedback: Batch limit exhaustion produces queueable failure errors rather than clearing mapped attributes from unified profile records.

options.text: The setup action reapplied the standard package schema, replacing bespoke mappings with default field relationships.
options.coachingFeedback: Standard data kit deployment forcefully resets existing mapping metadata, replacing customized enterprise entity relationships with package baseline specifications.

options.text: The platform integration user was suspended during package initialization due to permission set conflicts.
options.coachingFeedback: A suspended integration user halts ingestion entirely, whereas the streams remained active while mappings reverted to defaults.

stages.scenario: The team must configure Marketing Cloud Next streams while safeguarding existing custom data model extensions. Company policy requires all metadata modifications to pass through audited source control pipelines. Which installation pattern should the architect establish?

options.text: Deploy the full Sales Data Kit into a secondary data space and build formula fields to replicate mappings.
options.coachingFeedback: Creating formula fields in parallel data spaces adds unnecessary transformation overhead and fails to protect existing core model mappings.

options.text: Ingest required data kit streams individually through the Data Streams interface and apply field mappings selectively.
options.coachingFeedback: Selective stream ingestion isolates package dependencies, allowing teams to adopt standard messaging fields without overwriting customized enterprise entity mappings.

options.text: Recreate custom fields directly on standard data lake objects and assign them system administrator permissions.
options.coachingFeedback: Customizing standard lake object fields without governed model mapping does not route data into unified data model entities.

stages.scenario: During sandbox testing, all stream field labels defaulted to German because the background Integration User was provisioned with German locale settings. The business requires English metadata labels across all downstream tooling before promoting to production. Which cutover sequence resolves this constraint?

options.text: Reprovision the lower environment with English locale settings before package installation and promote verified metadata through version control.
options.coachingFeedback: Integration user locale settings become immutable upon data stream initialization, making pre-installation environment provisioning mandatory for clean label promotion.

options.text: Update the Integration User locale in company settings and execute an asynchronous schema refresh across all active streams.
options.coachingFeedback: Changing user language in platform settings does not alter established metadata labels on previously initialized data lake objects.

options.text: Apply custom translation workbench overrides to data lake object fields after deploying the data kit into production.
options.coachingFeedback: The Translation Workbench does not govern internal Data Cloud stream field labels displayed in downstream segmentation builders.

stages.scenario: The architect must detect unexpected data stream schema modifications or mapping regressions before they corrupt downstream segmentation and activation jobs. Which observability pattern should the delivery team implement?

options.text: Review setup audit trail logs on a weekly basis to identify administrative mapping changes after scheduled deployments.
options.coachingFeedback: Weekly audit reviews allow schema drift to persist for days, corrupting downstream calculated insights and marketing segment populations before discovery.

options.text: Implement automated CI/CD schema validation tests in pull requests and subscribe alerting webhooks to Data Stream error events.
options.coachingFeedback: Automated pull request validation detects schema drift before deployment, while event webhooks provide immediate notification when ingestion streams encounter mapping faults.

options.text: Enable comprehensive transaction logging across all platform flows and monitor storage usage via daily administrative reports.
options.coachingFeedback: Monitoring general platform flow logs produces excessive noise without providing targeted visibility into data stream mapping health.
